members.label: System 15
members.differences: The smallest of Behringer's three Eurorack copies of Moog's 1973 modular systems, after the System 15: two rows of 900-series modules with nothing wired between them.

members.label: System 35
members.differences: The middle size, after Moog's System 35: the same 900-series filters as the System 15, with more oscillators, amplifiers and envelopes to patch together.

members.label: System 55
members.differences: The largest, after Moog's System 55: the most modules of the three, among them the 960 sequential controller and the 962 sequential switch.

members.label: Moog Model 15
members.differences: Moog's own 1973 original: the smallest of its modular systems, in a portable suitcase-style case, with two oscillators, two VCAs and a low-pass filter. Behringer's System 15 keeps essentially the same choice of modules, made smaller with modern parts, and adds a MIDI-to-CV converter.

members.label: Moog System 35
members.differences: Moog's own 1973 original: a mid-sized modular system in a wedge-shaped housing, made for studios and teaching. Behringer's System 35 keeps essentially the same choice of modules, made smaller with modern parts, and adds a MIDI-to-CV converter.

members.label: Moog System 55
members.differences: Moog's own 1973 original: the largest of its modular systems, with the most modules Moog offered. Behringer's System 55 keeps essentially the same choice of modules, made smaller with modern parts, and adds a MIDI-to-CV converter.
